rows.basis: Growth in gross 'Servers and networking equipment' (172.492B − 113.156B = 59.336B), about 45% of 131.819B capex. This counts all server and network growth, AI and non-AI, net of retirements. It may include finance-leased assets and excludes datacenter shells (Land and buildings) and construction in progress. The earnings release says the capex increase 'primarily reflects investments in artificial intelligence' but gives no amount.

Growth in gross 'Equipment' (218.893B − 185.039B = 33.854B). Equipment is broader than servers: FY2024 Equipment equals Servers and networking 113.156B + Heavy equipment 52.228B + Other equipment 53.509B, so this includes fulfillment and logistics equipment. It is an upper bound on server growth, not an AI amount.

Growth in gross 'Equipment' (185.039B − 157.458B = 27.581B). It includes heavy and other fulfillment equipment as well as servers, and largely predates the AI buildout. It is all equipment growth, not an AI amount.

Growth in gross 'Equipment' (157.458B − 128.683B = 28.775B). It includes heavy and other fulfillment equipment as well as servers, and the year predates the generative-AI buildout. It is all equipment growth; the true AI share is likely much lower.

Amazon expects 'about $200 billion in capital expenditures across Amazon in 2026', citing AI, chips, robotics and satellites. That is total capex, not the AI part, and no AI split is given. Purchase commitments rose from 50.4B (FY2024) to 84.8B (FY2025), which is consistent with a larger buildout.

The MD&A expects technology and infrastructure spending to increase 'as we continue to add infrastructure and employees, including to support our artificial intelligence and machine learning initiatives'. There is no amount or share.
